questions.q: Where is the underlying Bank / Branch / Account structure actually maintained?
options: Inside Payables invoice setup
In Cash Management
In the General Ledger chart of accounts
In Procurement's supplier setup
questions.explain: Bank account setup is owned by Cash Management; Payables consumes it rather than duplicating it.

questions.q: What makes a Cash Management bank account eligible to fund Payables payments?
options: Being flagged for the "Payables Disbursements" account use
Having a specific minimum balance
Being the oldest account on record
Being denominated only in USD
questions.explain: A disbursement bank account is a Cash Management account specifically flagged for the Payables Disbursements use.

questions.q: What is the benefit of keeping bank account setup centralized in Cash Management rather than duplicated in each subledger?
options: It removes the need for any approvals
It automatically converts all currencies to USD
It allows one account record to serve disbursements, receipts, and reconciliation from a single source of truth
It eliminates the need for a Payment Process Profile
questions.explain: Centralizing bank account data avoids multiple disconnected copies drifting out of sync across subledgers.

questions.q: In the Solace Robotics example, which account funds payments for the European business unit?
options: Solace US Operating -- Checking (USD)
Solace EU Operating -- Current (EUR)
Both accounts equally, split 50/50
Neither -- European payments use a third account
questions.explain: The European business unit's payments route through the EUR-denominated Solace EU Operating account via its own PPP.

questions.q: Why do most organizations maintain more than one disbursement bank account?
options: Oracle requires a minimum of two accounts per tenant
Each invoice requires a newly created account
Each supplier needs its own dedicated account
Different currencies, business units, or control requirements often need separate accounts
questions.explain: Separate currencies, business units, and sometimes high-control disbursement needs typically drive multiple accounts.
